# WAS_Qmap { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap }

```python
WAS_Qmap()
```

Bias correction methods using quantile mapping techniques, adapted from
the R ``qmap`` package.

Provides fitting and application methods for empirical quantile mapping
(QUANT), robust quantile mapping (RQUANT), smoothing splines (SSPLIN),
parametric transformations (PTF) and distribution-based methods (DIST).
Methods optionally handle wet/dry day corrections and are designed for
precipitation or other non-negative variables.

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

- Inputs are expected to be non-negative.
- For gridded data, computations are performed column-wise (per grid cell).
- xarray support preserves coordinates and attributes.
- NaNs in observed / modeled data are filtered out at fit time. NaNs in
  the data passed to ``doQmap`` propagate to NaNs in the output.

| [doQmapPTF](#wass2s.WAS_Qmap.doQmapPTF) | Apply parametric transformation correction. |

| [doQmapSSPLIN](#wass2s.WAS_Qmap.doQmapSSPLIN) | Apply PCHIP-based quantile mapping correction. |
| [evaluate_bias_correction](#wass2s.WAS_Qmap.evaluate_bias_correction) | Evaluate bias correction performance. |
| [fitQmap](#wass2s.WAS_Qmap.fitQmap) | Fit a bias correction model using the specified quantile mapping method. |
| [fitQmapDIST](#wass2s.WAS_Qmap.fitQmapDIST) | Fit distribution-based quantile mapping. |

### doQmap { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.doQmap }

```python
WAS_Qmap.doQmap(x, fobj, **kwargs)
```

Apply the fitted bias correction to new data.

Returns the same array type as ``x`` and preserves its shape.

### doQmapDIST { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.doQmapDIST }

```python
WAS_Qmap.doQmapDIST(x, fobj)
```

Apply distribution-based bias correction.

### doQmapPTF { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.doQmapPTF }

```python
WAS_Qmap.doQmapPTF(x, fobj)
```

Apply parametric transformation correction.

### doQmapQUANT { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.doQmapQUANT }

```python
WAS_Qmap.doQmapQUANT(x, fobj, type='linear')
```

Apply empirical quantile mapping (QUANT).

Three regions are handled explicitly:
  - ``x < th_mod``      -> 0 (dry)
  - ``x > modq[-1]``    -> additive shift ``x + (fitq[-1] - modq[-1])``
    (constant-correction extrapolation for extremes)
  - otherwise           -> interpolation between ``modq`` and ``fitq``
NaN values in ``x`` are preserved as NaN in the output.

### doQmapRQUANT { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.doQmapRQUANT }

```python
WAS_Qmap.doQmapRQUANT(x, fobj, type='linear', slope_bound=(0.0, np.inf))
```

Apply RQUANT correction with slope-bounded extrapolation.

### doQmapSSPLIN { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.doQmapSSPLIN }

```python
WAS_Qmap.doQmapSSPLIN(x, fobj)
```

Apply PCHIP-based quantile mapping correction.

### evaluate_bias_correction { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.evaluate_bias_correction }

```python
WAS_Qmap.evaluate_bias_correction(
    obs,
    mod,
    corrected,
    wet_threshold=0.1,
    extreme_quantiles=(0.95, 0.99),
    time_dim=None,
)
```

Evaluate bias correction performance.

Returns a 2-tuple in both code paths so callers can unpack consistently.

- xarray inputs  -> ``(ds_dry_wet, ds_extreme)`` of xarray Datasets.
- numpy inputs   -> ``(dict_dry_wet, dict_extreme)``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type   | Description                                                                                                                | Default   |
|----------|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| time_dim | str    | Name of the time dimension for xarray inputs. If ``None`` it is taken from ``obs.dims[0]`` so any naming convention works. | `None`    |

### fitQmap { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.fitQmap }

```python
WAS_Qmap.fitQmap(obs, mod, method, **kwargs)
```

Fit a bias correction model using the specified quantile mapping method.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                           | Description                                                                                                                           | Default    |
|----------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| obs      | array_like or xarray.DataArray | Observed and modeled data of identical shape. Arrays may be 1D (time), 2D (time, grid) or 3D (T, Y, X). xarray DataArrays must be 3D. | _required_ |
| mod      | array_like or xarray.DataArray | Observed and modeled data of identical shape. Arrays may be 1D (time), 2D (time, grid) or 3D (T, Y, X). xarray DataArrays must be 3D. | _required_ |
| method   | str                            | One of ``'QUANT'``, ``'RQUANT'``, ``'SSPLIN'``, ``'PTF'``, ``'DIST'`` (case-insensitive).                                             | _required_ |
| **kwargs |                                | Forwarded to the underlying ``fitQmap*`` method.                                                                                      | `{}`       |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type   | Description                                                       |
|--------|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | dict   | Fitted object with parameters, ``class`` identifier and metadata. |

### fitQmapDIST { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.fitQmapDIST }

```python
WAS_Qmap.fitQmapDIST(obs, mod, distr='berngamma', qstep=None, **kwargs)
```

Fit distribution-based quantile mapping.

Uses a Bernoulli for wet/dry occurrence plus a continuous distribution
for the positive (wet) values.

### fitQmapPTF { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.fitQmapPTF }

```python
WAS_Qmap.fitQmapPTF(
    obs,
    mod,
    transfun='power',
    parini=None,
    cost='RSS',
    wet_day=False,
    qstep=None,
)
```

Fit a parametric transformation function (PTF).

### fitQmapQUANT { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.fitQmapQUANT }

```python
WAS_Qmap.fitQmapQUANT(obs, mod, wet_day=False, qstep=0.01, nboot=1)
```

Fit empirical quantile mapping with optional bootstrap of obs.

### fitQmapRQUANT { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.fitQmapRQUANT }

```python
WAS_Qmap.fitQmapRQUANT(obs, mod, wet_day=True, qstep=0.01, nlls=10, nboot=10)
```

Robust quantile mapping with local linear fits.

### fitQmapSSPLIN { #wass2s.WAS_Qmap.fitQmapSSPLIN }

```python
WAS_Qmap.fitQmapSSPLIN(obs, mod, wet_day=False, qstep=0.01)
```

Fit quantile mapping using PCHIP smoothing splines.
